cells.tense: You're knowing it now, and you're not arguing with yourself about it.
cells.verb: recognizing what matters before you can say why
cells.place: standing in the middle of what you're attending to
cells.ask: offer someone the shape of what you see — the frame that makes the tangle make sense — and let the structure serve what it holds.
cells.core: You can tell what matters before you can explain it, and it turns out to be right. You don't need the whole picture to know which part to pick up, and you don't flinch when you don't know yet — the not-knowing is comfortable instead of frightening. What you notice lands without having to win an argument, which is why people feel steadier around you than they can account for.
cells.sheetLine: You see straight to what matters, and you're easy about the parts you can't see yet.

cells.tense: You're bracing against a future where you still haven't got it figured out.
cells.verb: collecting more before you'll let yourself know
cells.place: behind a wall you've been calling preparation
cells.ask: let one thing you're drawn toward actually start — take one step toward the light without testing first whether it's the right star.
cells.core: You're gathering. One more piece, one more angle, one more thing read before you'll allow yourself to say what you already sense — and the gathering has become the wall. The knowing is right there under the pile and you keep adding to the pile so you don't have to stand behind what's under it. You wanted certainty, and the wanting has cost you the thing certainty was for.
cells.sheetLine: The gathering has become the wall.

cells.tense: You stopped trusting what you saw a while back, and you're still standing there.
cells.verb: asking someone else what you already sense
cells.place: at a door you already walked through
cells.ask: let one uncertain thing stay uncertain and take the next step by the light you have — what comes back will tell you whether your sight can be trusted.
cells.core: You used to just know, and somewhere along the way that got taken away from you — contested, corrected, overruled enough times that you stopped offering it. Now you check with other people before you'll let yourself see, and the checking keeps coming back wrong because it's looking in the wrong place. What's missing isn't insight. It's your willingness to be the one who has it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep asking out loud for what you already see.

cells.tense: You're already perceiving clearly and calling it luck.
cells.verb: seeing through to the essence and crediting the coincidence
cells.place: in a room you're already writing in
cells.ask: trace one choice you called random back to the moment you first saw it, and give that moment back to yourself.
cells.core: You keep noticing the right thing at the right time and then explaining it away. The insight is doing the steering — it picked the direction, it skipped the dead end, it knew who to call — and you're describing it as intuition or accident or being lucky. The knowing is running. You just haven't put your name on it.
cells.sheetLine: You've been seeing straight this whole time and calling it luck.
